candidates.speaker: Alister McGrath
candidates.proposedProposition: Religious belief can be a defensible interpretation of public evidence without claiming privileged knowledge, proof, or certainty, because every worldview rests on contestable judgments of explanation.
candidates.attributionBasis: McGrath explicitly begins a response and delivers the final substantive argument, using first-person qualifications about interpretation and faith until his closing thanks.
candidates.loadBearingReason: This is the pro side's concluding defense of religious intellectual credibility, reframing faith as an open and contestable explanatory judgment rather than inaccessible special knowledge.
